music.a: Albuquerque's top music venues include Sister Bar for indie and local acts, Popejoy Hall for classical and Broadway shows, the historic KiMo Theatre, Sunshine Theater, and El Rey Theater. Larger outdoor concerts happen at Balloon Fiesta Park and Isleta Amphitheater.

sports.a: Albuquerque is home to the Isotopes (Triple-A baseball) at Isotopes Park and UNM Lobos basketball at The Pit arena. The city also hosts road races, cycling events, wrestling, and mixed martial arts throughout the year.

arts-theater.q: What are the best arts and theater venues in Albuquerque?
arts-theater.a: Top venues include the KiMo Theatre (a stunning 1920s Pueblo Deco landmark), Popejoy Hall at UNM, Albuquerque Little Theatre, and the Albuquerque Museum. Old Town galleries and Nob Hill studios also host rotating exhibitions.

arts-theater.q: Are there free art events in Albuquerque?

festivals.q: What are the biggest festivals in Albuquerque?
festivals.a: The Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta in October is the world's largest hot air balloon event. Other major festivals include the New Mexico State Fair at Expo New Mexico, the Gathering of Nations Powwow, and the New Mexico Wine Festival.

outdoor.a: Albuquerque offers guided hikes in the Sandia Mountains, river cleanups along the Rio Grande, cycling events on the Paseo del Bosque trail, and stargazing nights at Petroglyph National Monument. The high desert setting makes outdoor events accessible year-round.
